newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 falls as foreign buyers remain absent.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 falls as foreign buyers remain absent.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index moved lower on Monday with dealers blaming an absence of foreign buying orders and a lack of fresh factors generally for the stagnant picture on the equities market.
The PX50 lost 2.8 points, 0.5 percent, to 540.6 while the major issue dominated RPIX was virtually unchanged on 1,128.7.
"It's stagnation I would say. We have no orders from foreign players," said Petr Opocensky of Citicorp Securities.

Opocensky added that the market was desperate for some new influences, such as the cut in interest rates which has been speculated upon by the money markets for several weeks but has so far failed to materialise.

The most prolific mover of the day was Tabak which is 77 percent owned by Philip Morris. Tabak, a notoriously illiquid share which is therefore prone to wild swings, dropped 417 crowns, 4.9 percent, to 7,928.
Power utility CEZ also fell, dropping 10 crowns to 1,030. SPT Telecom was unchanged on 3,301 and Komercni Banka rose 24 crowns to 2,250.
Turnover remained low, though slightly higher than Friday, at just one billion crowns.
